description: GalacticGeeks is a multidisciplinary team united by a shared interest in using technology to better understand complex problems in our world and beyond. Our team brings together expertise in AI engineering, AI research, data engineering, frontend development, and visual design, allowing us to approach problems from both technical and creative perspectives.
summary: AtmoSpy is a multi agent system, built by team GalacticGeeks, where a team of ten AI agents investigates how Earth is changing using real NASA satellite data, and answers four questions: what changed, where, by how much, and whether the change is statistically significant. It helps students, educators and curious citizens explore NASA data without needing to code or know statistics, with guided "Detect" steps, plain-language definitions and downloadable notebooks to reproduce every result. Under the hood, a deterministic Python core computes every number from 26 NASA variables (MERRA-2, GPM IMERG, AIRS, OMI, GLDAS and POWER), using autocorrelation-corrected Mann–Kendall trend tests and false-discovery-rate control; the AI agents only plan the work and word the findings, a guardrail rejects any figure that doesn't trace back to the data, and a Skeptic agent challenges each result before it is shown. Try it now at https://atmospy.vercel.app/.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS:

AtmoSpy is a team of ten AI agents that investigates how Earth is changing using real NASA data, and answers four questions with real numbers: what changed, where, how much, and whether the change is statistically significant (and whether significant also means important). Users can: (1) press "Discover" to scan 16 region-and-variable pairs in parallel, ranked by criteria shown on screen; (2) ask a plain-language question such as "Has temperature changed significantly in the Tibetan Plateau since 1990?" and watch the agents work live; (3) follow a guided four-question "Detect" path built for students; (4) test every available variable over a region at once; (5) subscribe to a "Watch" that re-runs on a schedule; and (6) download any finding as a Jupyter notebook that recomputes the result. The project has two layers that never mix. A deterministic Python core computes every number from 26 variables across six NASA datasets (MERRA-2, GPM IMERG, GLDAS, AIRS, OMI, NASA POWER). A language model only plans the investigation and words the result, and a guardrail rejects any number in its output that doesn't trace back to the data.

BENEFITS:

Anyone can explore NASA Earth data without coding or statistics training. Results are honest about uncertainty: a Skeptic agent argues against each finding, a real trend that isn't significant yet is reported as exactly that (with the years of data needed), and effect size is shown separately from p-values. Everything is reproducible and open source.

INTENDED IMPACT:

To build data and science literacy for students, teachers, journalists and citizens, and to help scientists quickly triage where in the world change is real rather than noise. It shows that AI can help people investigate evidence without inventing any of it.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY:

Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy and Postgres (Supabase in production); NumPy, SciPy, pandas, statsmodels, pymannkendall, ruptures, xarray and Zarr for the science; Groq API with GPT OSS 120B for planning and wording; Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind, three.js, MapLibre, React Flow, Recharts and Framer Motion for the interface; Vercel and Render for hosting; GitHub Actions CI (about 170 backend tests plus a browser smoke test with an automated accessibility audit). Built on ordinary laptops, with no special hardware or GPU. We also used Claude Code as a coding assistant (see "Use of AI").

HOW IT IS CREATIVE:

The landing page is a living 3D island where the agents act out a real investigation, passing a glowing orb of NASA data from agent to agent. Each finding includes a pixel-art "then vs now" scene whose size follows the effect size, not just the p-value. The adversarial Skeptic agent, and the rule that the AI can describe numbers but never create them, make the system trustworthy by design. It also detects "same cause, opposite directions" patterns, such as the troposphere warming while the stratosphere cools.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED:

Statistical honesty: we remove the seasonal cycle and correct for autocorrelation, chosen by a Monte Carlo test (about 5 to 9% false positives, versus about 30% for the plain test), and we control for testing many things at once. Region averages are area-weighted and need at least 70% coverage. We label reanalysis and model data as such, not as direct measurements. Data licensing and citation (every finding shows its source and version, with BibTeX). Reliability: demos are frozen so they work even if the backend sleeps, and a rule-based fallback works without the AI. Accessibility: keyboard support, screen-reader labels, reduced-motion support and colour-blind-safe charts, with known gaps (no audio, mouse-driven 3D scene, English only). AtmoSpy is not an official NASA product.
